transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. It must stay out of use until a qualified appliance engineer has checked it. The usual causes are a leak around the door (seal, door alignment or a spray arm being obstructed), a loose/split inlet or drain-hose connection, or an internal hose/pump/sump leak. If there is lots of foam, washing-up liquid or excess detergent can also force water out of the door. 1. Keep people away from the wet area and mop up only if you can do so without going near the sockets. Do not pull out the plug or reset anything while it is wet.
2. Look for foam at the door or on the floor. Foam points strongly to incorrect/too much detergent rather than a failed part.
3. Once the area is dry enough to look safely, check whether water has tracked from the door edge, the inlet/drain hose connections under the sink, or from beneath the machine. That location is the key clue: door edge suggests seal/spray/loading; hose connection suggests plumbing; underneath suggests an internal leak. Do not run a test cycle to find it. The engineer can safely isolate, locate the source and check for water damage around the electrics.

theres loads of bubbles coming out the door and it smells lemony, my housemate put fairy liquid in cos we ran out of tablets. its still running and the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. what do i do??

The Fairy liquid is the cause of the bubbles and overflow — it makes far more foam than a dishwasher can contain. Do not try to cancel it at the dishwasher or move the extension lead while there is water nearby. If the circuit has not already been isolated at the consumer unit, do that now only if you can reach it without stepping in or reaching across water. If water reaches the extension lead/socket, or there is any crackling, heat, burning smell or tripping, treat it as urgent: leave the area and call an emergency electrician; call 999 if there is immediate danger of fire or electric shock. Once the electrics and area have been made safe, the dishwasher must stay off and not be used again until a qualified appliance engineer has checked it. The foam itself is usually not a failed seal or pump, but water near sockets/extension leads means the appliance and surrounding electrics need checking before any attempt to rinse the suds out.
ok the fuse box is in the hallway, not near the water. i turned the dishwasher off at the wall switch and theres no crackling or burning smell. should i just flip the power off at the fuse box?

Yes — if you can identify the dishwasher/kitchen-socket circuit at the fuse box, switch that circuit off now. As the consumer unit is away from the water, this is the safest way to ensure the dishwasher and nearby sockets are isolated. Do not touch the dishwasher plug, wall switch, sockets or extension lead while there is water or dampness around them. The likely cause is the Fairy liquid: it creates excessive foam, which forces water and suds out around the door. That does not by itself prove a failed seal or pump, but because water has spread towards electrical equipment, the dishwasher must not be used again until a qualified appliance engineer has checked it, and any affected socket/extension lead should be checked by an electrician before use. Only mop water where you can do so without touching or approaching the sockets, plug or lead. Do not attempt a rinse, drain or restart cycle to clear the foam.
